VRChat SDK works by processing data, bundling it into an AssetBundle, and uploading it. They do not store the original source files anywhere on their server, and it would make no sense to, considering those files can easy become multiple gigabytes big. It's possible to extract some of that data into some intermediate form from the application cache, but if you have the technical skills to do that, you have the technical skills to properly back up your data in the first place.
The only real thing you can do here is take it as a hard lesson learned: backup your data. Source files can be saved into a synced folder with OneDrive/Dropbox or other similar service. They are free and will automatically keep everything backed up for you.

@{62e1338f5d95dd469bfc8f94|full_name}: this is just blatantly wrong the future proofing check box uploads the full unity package and previously we could download the package you can even message support to get files back its just a nightmare to do so. People are looking for a user friendly solution. However with future proofing off all you would get is an asset bundle which with the right know how even that is recoverable.

@{6067b5f271b99e7e34dcd948|full_name}: I did not know that, Interesting.

But this doesn't really solve the OP's problem. I doubt that those who don't know how to perform any kind of backup will have ticked this box.

Salvaging usable source files from asset bundles depends heavily on how the original model was made; there is no user-friendly solution here. The data stored in them is the bare minimum: vertices, normals, weights, uvs, triangle lists etc. You won't be able to recover any modifiers or any other sources of generated geometry.

A user-friendly solution would either consist of a new feature (e.g. built into the Creator Companion) that would reliably store source assets, or simple education—saving your files in a synced cloud folder is very user friendly.

@{62e1338f5d95dd469bfc8f94|full_name}: or re-enabling the links we could use to download our avatar packages for like 3 years prior (or asset bundles since both links existed) and attaching that link to a nice button in our avatar lists on the main vrchat site since the asset bundle and if future proofed unity package links are created on upload. 

As for rebuilding from asset bundles its something many of us did for 2ish years before the package links became the more common way to dl our files by talking to the api. 

We can excuse a massive oversight and say its too hard or acknowledge 95% of the system is already built... Recovery through asset bundles can bring back almost everything except shaders as well. 3 of my avatars were rebuilt from asset bundles because I can no longer get the bases I used to build them since the gumroad links are gone for the base and the original creators no longer have the files.

If you know how to pull apart asset bundles you can get fbxs textures and prefabs.

Prefabs of course would include your phys bones coliders recievers etc. 

Shaders are the only thing that you have to really rebuild.

The other crazy idea is just making the default state for uploads future proofed

@{6067b5f271b99e7e34dcd948|full_name}: I think it's fair to ask for links for your own uploaded content. I suppose anything is better than nothing if you've lost everything.

I think they may be hesitant to enable the future proof thing by default if it works the way you describe. Source files for some avatars and worlds can easily run hundreds of megabytes to multiple gigabytes. I shudder thinking about the storage and bandwidth requirements given the amount of content routinely uploaded free of charge.

@{62e1338f5d95dd469bfc8f94|full_name}: if size or bandwidth is the concern it would make more sense to hard cap an account to a certain data limit and say you can have 20 gb of content rather than beat around the bush.

 The best way too handle that is to figure out the biggest issue and be clear and concise on it. If it was data or bandwith issue a cap makes more sense rather than causing a massive recovery issue to save file sizes. 

If its a issue with logistics for file recovery I question the competancy of the team given that the team already has a system for it built. 

If its simply that they don't want to do it or find it unimportant than just say it. Transparency is key.

Oh its important to mention as well a 20gb set of source files like my personal avatars when converted to a normal unity package can be as little as 8 mb its not a copy of the source.

This can vary wildly no different than the assetbundles sometimes the asset bundles are larger than unity packages it just depends

details:
There should been a way to recover avatar and/or world thru your logged in account.
And yes, they should have backed up their files but not every knows how to properly back up said files. 
When their project gets corrupted or their PC gets a hard crash and lost all their files. They got literally nothing to retrieve their files back from the only source left….which is the VRChat who gets a copy from uploads
Users should not have to go thru ripping their own avatars and/or worlds only to get banned for ripping their on work.
The community I’m in had a long time user since 2018 who had lost her files to her avatars that were uploaded. All her avatars has her name in plain bold text. 
She ripped those avatars just to re-obtain them but until recently, she gets banned from ripping her own models. 
That had cause an uproar within the Veteran members of the community and most that are getting to know her work in defending her choice to her avatars….
And I’ve already heard from some users who have lost their work and lost the will to re-create.
If VRChat is for the community. 
Then there should be a way to protect those “Will to Create”
